program.help:
Extract spikes using the spatial derivative across probe channels to suppress common-mode noise before threshold detection.
The script is a drop-in replacement for ndm_extractspikes. Its detection step applies a spatial derivative across the ordered channels of each electrode group before evaluating whether the signal exceeds the threshold. Because genuine spike currents are spatially localised while motion artefacts and electrical interference are correlated across all contacts, the derivative enhances single-unit signals relative to noise.
Detection (threshold crossing + peak search) operates entirely on the spatial-derivative signal. Waveform extraction writes the ORIGINAL, un-differentiated data to the .spk files so that downstream PCA and clustering see raw amplitudes — exactly as they would with ndm_extractspikes.
CHANNEL ORDERING Channels in each spikeDetection group should be listed in their physical probe order (tip-to-base, or shank-proximal to shank-distal) so that spatial neighbours are adjacent in the channel list.
PARAMETERS
# thresholdFactor
Threshold = thresholdFactor × 4σ, where σ is the Quiroga (2004) noise estimate computed from the SPATIAL DERIVATIVE of the signal over the baseline window: σ = median(|sdiff|) / 0.6745
# refractoryPeriod
Minimum number of samples between consecutive spikes.
# peakSearchLength
Length of the peak-search window (in samples).
# start
Starting point in the file (in s) for computation of the baseline noise level.
# duration
Duration (in s) for computation of the baseline noise level.
# sdiffOrder
Order of the spatial derivative: 0 — none (equivalent to ndm_extractspikes; no spatial filtering) 1 — first-order difference: s[i] = x[i] − x[i+1] 2 — discrete Laplacian (default): s[i] = x[i] − ½(x[i−1] + x[i+1]) (edge channels use one-sided differences)
